'''Bengel Morr''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who was the [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Orgus Din]] during the [[Great Galactic War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]]. Morr was present in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] when the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sacking of Coruscant|attacked]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[3653 BBY]], and the devastation drove the gentle Nautolan insane. Turning to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and becoming determined to destroy the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] took on an apprentice by the name of [[Callef]] and followed the him when the Order migrated to their recently rediscovered homeworld of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]. There, the two [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] marshaled the native [[Flesh Raider]]s into an army and [[Flesh Raider uprising|attacked]] both the Jedi Order and the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Pilgrims]] who had settled on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]].

However, Callef was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by a [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi]] during an early [[Attack on the Gnarls Outpost|assault]] on the Order, and Morr soon learned that his former Master decided to take on the initiate as a Padawan. Din and his new student worked to uncover the truth behind the Flesh Raiders' attacks, and despite the blows struck against his army by the Jedi Order managed to capture Din with the help of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] villagers. Bringing the Jedi Master before the ancient machine known as the [[Vur Tepe|Forge]], Morr prepared to kill his former teacher, but Din's apprentice confronted the Nautolan and [[Battle of the Forge|defeated]] him in battle.

Healed of his insanity by the [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Temple]] healers, Morr embraced the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] once more and was [[Jedi training/Legends|retrained]] as a Jedi Padawan. When the [[Galactic War]] broke out across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], Morr was sent to the battlefields of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], where he served under Din's apprentice&mdash;now the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the Hero of Tython. Fighting alongside the forces of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]], Morr and his fellow Jedi aided their commander in stopping the fallen Jedi [[Tol Braga]] from massacring thousands of civilians, and their actions during the [[Battle of Corellia]] helped ensure a Republic victory.

==Biography==
{{Quote|I'm sorry to tell you, Orgus, but the Senate voted to put off the rebuilding of the Temple.''"<br />"''Perhaps that's for the best&hellip; my Padawan was in there&hellip; |[[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Zym]] and Orgus Din|<ref name="The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 2: New Galactic Order">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 2: New Galactic Order]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Master_Orgus_Din.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Bengel Morr's Master Orgus Din]]
A [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], Bengel Morr was [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]] in the ways of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] by the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Orgus Din]] during the [[Great Galactic War]] with the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]].<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> When [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] forces under the command of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Angral]] assaulted the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] capital of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[3653 BBY]],<ref name="Threat of Peace 1">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 1: Treaty of Coruscant]]''</ref> an event later known as the [[Sacking of Coruscant]],<ref name="Timeline 1">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant|int=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant}}</ref> Morr was present in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] and witnessed [[Darth Malgus]]'s attack on the Temple firsthand. The devastation drove Morr insane, shattering the gentle Nautolan's psyche and making him blame the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Escaping the ruins of the Temple and hiding amidst the chaos on the capital, Morr learned that the Republic and the Jedi had submitted to the Empire's demands and signed the [[Treaty of Coruscant]].<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" />

Morr viewed the Treaty as cowardly and weak, fueling his hatred of the Jedi Order, and decided that he would have to destroy the Jedi in order to make them stronger. Turning to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and becoming a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]], Morr spent the next decade plotting the destruction of the Jedi. During this time, he recruited the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|human]] [[Callef]] as his apprentice, training the young man in the ways of the dark side.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" />

By [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Time">{{TOR dates|1}}</ref> Callef and Morr had followed the Order to [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], where the Jedi had retreated to following the treaty. There, hiding from the Order in the widely unexplored regions of the planet, the two Dark Jedi began to marshal the native [[Flesh Raider]]s into an army.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> Finding some of the savage and violent species to be Force-sensitive, Morr trained them to be [[Force Adept]]s,<ref name="Enemy Force">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Enemy Force|Tython}}</ref> and eventually commanded a significant fighting force under the leadership of the Flesh Raiders' [[Grand Chieftain]] [[Keshk]].<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Weapon of the Jedi|Tython}}</ref> As his forces became stronger, Morr encouraged the natives to become more bold in their attacks upon both the Jedi and the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Pilgrims|settlers]] of [[Kalikori village]], a settlement in the [[Tythos Ridge]].<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

===War on Tython===
In [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Time" /> Morr decided the time was right to strike. He ordered Callef to take an invasion force through one of the tunnels connecting the Flesh Raider-controlled [[Tythos Ridge]] to the [[Tythonian Gnarls]], a region north of the [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Jedi Temple]] with only a small outpost. Callef's mission was to [[Attack on the Gnarls Outpost|destroy]] the outpost as a test of the Flesh Raiders' combat skills, but Morr's plans went awry when Callef was [[Duel in the Gnarls cave|killed]] by a [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi]] who had just arrived on the planet.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Attack of the Flesh Raiders|Tython}}</ref> Angered at the loss of his friend and student, Morr observed the apprentice's actions from afar<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> and watched as his former Master Orgus Din took the Jedi on as his Padawan.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

Under Morr's leadership, the Flesh Raiders continued to step up their attacks and began establishing camps across the planet. One such camp was based near the ruins of [[Kaleth]], an ancient temple-city of the Jedi's predecessors, the [[Je'daii Order]], and Morr instructed those among the group who were Force-sensitive to travel to a nearby [[Ancient shrine|meditation shrine]] to learn from a [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] which he gave them. Morr was unconcerned when the group was [[Skirmish at the ancient shrine|eliminated]] by Din's new apprentice, but began to grow concerned when the scouts of Kalikori Village discovered one of his command bases in the Tythos Ridge.

When Din's Padawan [[Raid on the Tythos Ridge shield generator|shut down]] the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] protecting the camp in order for Din and the other Masters to destroy the base, Morr decided to contact the young Jedi from another secure base. Communicating via [[Holocomm/Legends|holocomm]], the Dark Jedi expressed his displeasure with the apprentice's actions and warned that he would destroy the Jedi Order no matter what. During the Jedi assault, Morr dispatched a team of Flesh Raider saboteurs to attack Kalikori, where they planted [[Poison/Legends|toxin]] mines in the village's crop fields until Din's apprentice deactivated them.

At the command base, the Masters discovered the locations of a number of other camps across the surface of the planet, and were forced to mobilize almost all of the Knights at the Temple in order to take them all out at once. Despite this, Morr was not concerned&mdash;he ordered his subordinate Keshk to gather part of the army at the ruins of [[Vur Tepe]], another Je'daii city, and prepare for an assault on the soon-to-be relatively unprotected Jedi Temple. Morr himself took advantage of Din and the Padawan's own missions to destroy two bases by approaching the villagers of Kalikori with an offer: give him Orgus Din, and Morr would order his forces to spare the village from any further attacks. The villagers, who had been on bad terms with the Jedi as a result of the Order's refusal of aid, agreed to his offer and sent out a false [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]] knowing that Din was nearby.

[[File:Battle_of_the_Forge.png|thumb|left|200px|Morr has his former master at his mercy.]]
Din obligingly walked straight into the trap, ordering his apprentice to return to the village just before he himself arrived. Caught off guard, the Jedi Master was quickly subdued by Morr's Flesh Raider bodyguards. However, Morr changed his mind before departing and demanded the life of Din's apprentice as well&mdash;forcing the villagers to try and capture the young Padawan. Morr and his bodyguards took their captive through the Flesh Raider-controlled [[Tythos Ridge]] to an ancient site known as the [[Vur Tepe|Forge]], which had been used by both the ancient and modern Jedi to construct and repair their weapons. There, his subordinate [[Keshk]] marshaled what was left of the Flesh Raider army in preparation for an attack on the Jedi while Morr prepared his Force Adepts in case someone tried to rescue Din.

Fortunately, Din's Padawan was able to escape from the villagers without violence and learned of Morr's location from Kalikori's [[Matriarch/Legends|Matriarch]] [[Ranna Tao'Ven]].

===The road back===
{{Quote|I owe you a debt. No, more than that. I owe you my life.|Bengel Morr, in a holomessage to the Hero of Tython|<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
Thanks to the Jedi healers, Morr's sanity was restored, and he was cleansed of the taint of the dark side that had clouded him since the Sacking of Coruscant. He would remain at the Temple for quite some time, slowly retraining in the ways of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] under the guidance of the Masters. As he continued to progress, Morr decided to contact the apprentice who had saved him. He recorded a holomessage thanking the Jedi, now a Knight, for sparing him and allowing Morr to redeem himself.<ref name="Message 1">{{TORcite|Ship Holorecording 1 from Bengel Morr}}</ref> The Nautolan would continue to send messages to the Knight, explaining how it felt to recover. Morr felt at ease communicating with the Knight, as the young Jedi had witnessed him at his worst moments,<ref name="Message 2">{{TORcite|Ship Holorecording 2 from Bengel Morr}}</ref> and felt that his greatest regret was being unable to apologize to his former master.<ref name="Message 1" /> Morr also came to realize that it was truly his fault that his friend and apprentice Callef was dead, and he was able to forgive the Knight for killing the young man.<ref name="Message 2" />

When the Knight returned to Tython with Lord [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]] after escaping from the [[Emperor's Fortress|space station]] of the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]],<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|An Unthinkable Alliance|the Emperor's Space Station}}</ref> Morr attempted to speak with the Jedi, but the Council ensured that no one spoke with the pair. He heard several different rumors at the Temple after the Knight's departure, with some saying that the Knight had fallen to the dark side and was looking for redemption, while others believed that the Jedi had never fallen and had instead captured Lord Scourge. Morr was simply relieved to learn that the Knight was alive, as Master [[Tol Braga]]'s [[Jedi strike team (capture of the Sith Emperor)|strike team]] had failed to reported back and were believed dead, and sent a third message to the Jedi expressing his relief.<ref name="Message 3">{{TORcite|Ship Holorecording 3 from Bengel Morr}}</ref>

===The Battle of Corellia===
{{Quote|Do you ever wonder if I prepared you for this? Perhaps the Force guided me to attack you on Tython.''"<br />"''Destiny always looks clearer in hindsight."''<br />"''I want to believe all the pain I caused wasn't for nothing.|Morr and the Hero of Tython|<ref name="SWTOR" />}}
[[File:Morr_fight_Mando.png|250px|thumb|Bengel Morr faces [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]].]]
As the [[Galactic War]] ignited across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], Morr was among those Padawans and Knights on Tython who were sent to aid the Republic forces on the planet of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. While Morr's training was not yet complete, Council member [[Jaric Kaedan]] decided that he was ready and assigned Morr to the care of three Jedi Masters. However, the four were ambushed in [[Coronet City/Legends|Coronet City's]] [[Blastfield Shipyards]] by a group of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] hired by the Empire, and Morr was forced to watch as the three Masters were cut down by the mercenaries. The Padawan evaded the Mandalorians until they cornered him in the [[Rusty Freighter Cantina]], located in the [[Red Light Sector (Corellia)|Red Light Sector's]] [[Entertainment Plaza]]. Barricading himself in the [[Cantina/Legends|cantina's]] VIP lounge, Morr fought off the Mandalorians that came to face him alone or in pairs.<ref name="Jedi Commander" />

However, Morr was rescued by the Hero of Tython, who was searching for the remaining Jedi on the planet. Taking the Mandalorians by surprise, the Knight eliminated the attackers in the main cantina and entered the building's VIP lounge to witness Morr quickly dispatch the last two mercenaries.<ref name="Jedi Commander" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Bengel was strong in the Force, and the most gentle being I've ever known.|Orgus Din|<ref name="SWTOR" />}}
A male Nautolan with black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and light blue skin, Bengel Morr was a gentle and kind person in his early life. However, the horrific attack on the Jedi Temple devastated Morr's psyche, driving him insane.<ref name="Enemy Force" /> As he fled into the underlevels of Coruscant to escape the Sith, Morr gave into fear&mdash;an emotion that quickly became anger when he learned that the Jedi and the Republic had submitted to the Sith and signed the Treaty of Coruscant. Morr turned to the dark side and spent the next decade plotting the destruction of the Order,<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> and his only friend during this time was his student Callef.<ref name="Message 2" /> The two bonded over the shared hatred of the Order, which Morr had instilled in the young man during his training, and Morr became a calmer and more calculating figure compared to his fiery and proud student.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> The Nautolan's belief in his victory became absolute thanks to years of planning, and he maintained a calm demeanor when Callef fell at the hands of Din's new apprentice.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" />

Morr's anger at the Sith in the aftermath of the Sacking was transformed by his insanity into a belief that the Jedi were weak, and he desired to destroy the Order. However, Master Din realized that Morr was not a Sith himself&mdash;he wished to rebuild the Jedi into something that could destroy the Sith.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> When he was defeated by Din's apprentice at the Forge, Morr believed that the Force had acted through him to forge the other Jedi into the perfect weapon. The Dark Jedi was more than willing to submit and offer the Padawan his knowledge and power, but instead he was defeated and brought back to the Order for healing.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

Healed of his insanity by the Jedi, Morr was retrained as a Jedi Padawan and learned to confront his emotions.<ref name="Message 1" /> He regretted causing Callef's death through his own arrogance and hatred, and also that he never got to apologize to his Master before Din's death. Morr also developed a friendship with Din's other apprentice, seeing similarities between himself and the young Knight:<ref name="Message 2" /> the pair's training under Din,<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> their fall to the dark side and redemption,<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" /> and the loss of close friends during times of war, as well as the bond felt by Morr after the events at the Forge.<ref name="Message 3" /> Fighting in the Battle of Corellia reminded Morr of his time as a Dark Jedi, but the Hero of Tython reassured the Nautolan that he had changed for the better since then.<ref name="Jedi Commander" />

==Powers and abilities==
Morr was a formidable lightsaber duelist and Force-user, able to control the violent Flesh Raiders and train the Force-sensitives among them in the ways of the Force. However, his combat skills were not enough to defeat Master Din's apprentice even with years of experience and the advantage of wielding a lightsaber. He would later be retrained in the ways of the light side by the Jedi Order, and serve alongside many Jedi Knights on the battlefields of Corellia.

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|When I heard about the fighting on Corellia, I knew they'd send you. And now my patience is rewarded. Look at you. You're everything I ever hoped you'd become, Weapon of the Jedi.|Bengel Morr, if the player released him on Tython|<ref name="SWTOR" />}}
Bengel Morr was created for ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Wikipedia:Massively mulitplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] on [[December 20]], [[2011]]. He serves as the primary antagonist of the Jedi Knight class' storyline on Tython during the Prelude, though was not explicitly named as such until the mission "The Face of the Enemy". After defeating him on Tython, a dark side Jedi can either release him to "prepare the galaxy" or execute him. If released, he will give the Knight the knowledge to build a slightly better lightsaber and a series of increasingly disturbing audio messages (available on the player's ship) as the class campaign progresses.

In his initial appearance in [[T7-O1|T7-01's]] holorecording of him speaking with Callef, his obscured face is that of a [[Human/Legends|human]] rather than a Nautolan.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

The character of Morr was voiced by [[Victor Slezak]].{{Fact}}
